about: Substances of the Bench's reaction show records (I-054, docs/loop/items/I-054/spec.md). Generated by tools/chemdb/build_show_data.py; edit that script, not this file. dhf: standard enthalpy of formation at 298.15 K and 1 bar in kJ/mol per phase (s, l, g, aq); src names an entry of sources, verified false means entered from a printed table and not checked against a machine-readable copy, estimated true says how. state: the phase at 298.15 K and 1 atm. cp: NIST Shomate coefficients per phase, [[Tmin K, Tmax K, A, B, C, D, E], ...] with Cp = A + B T + C T^2 + D T^3 + E/T^2 in J/(mol K). colour: per phase, a described colour with its source; hex is an sRGB rendering of the description (hex_estimated), never a measurement; a colour with no hex is known but not rendered. grain: how a solid that forms in a solution settles.

sources.CRC-T: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 'Standard Thermodynamic Properties of Chemical Substances' (section 5), as tabulated in the chemicals package (https://github.com/CalebBell/chemicals, file 'CRC Standard Thermodynamic Properties of Chemical Substances.tsv').
sources.CRC-ION: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 'Thermodynamic Properties of Aqueous Ions' (section 5), as tabulated in the chemicals package (file 'CRC Thermodynamic Properties of Aqueous Ions.tsv'). A dissolved strong electrolyte is the sum of its ions at infinite dilution.
sources.CRC-PHYS: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 'Physical Constants of Inorganic Compounds' and 'Physical Constants of Organic Compounds' (melting point, boiling point, density), as tabulated in the chemicals package.
sources.CRC-PRINTED: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 'Physical Constants of Inorganic Compounds', the printed boiling or sublimation point (KCl boils at 1420 C; CaO at 2850 C; ZnS sublimes at 1185 C). Entered by hand (verified: false).
sources.CRC-PC: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, heat of fusion and heat of vaporization tables (section 6), as tabulated in the chemicals package.
sources.NIST-SHOMATE: NIST Chemistry WebBook (SRD 69), Shomate heat capacity coefficients per phase, as tabulated in the chemicals package (file 'webbook_shomate_coefficients.json'). Cp = A + B T + C T^2 + D T^3 + E / T^2 in J/(mol K), T in K.
sources.API-TDB: API Technical Data Book, gas-phase enthalpies of formation (Albahri), as tabulated in the chemicals package (file 'API TDB Albahri Hf (g).tsv').
sources.NBS82: Wagman et al., 'The NBS tables of chemical thermodynamic properties', J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data 11, Suppl. 2 (1982). Entered from the printed table (verified: false): not checked against a machine-readable copy; check at the science review.
sources.GHAZ: Enthalpies of vaporization at 298 K, appendix of Ghazerati et al., as tabulated in the chemicals package (file 'Ghazerati Appendix Vaporization Enthalpy.tsv').
sources.RDKIT: Computed: an RDKit 2026.09 ETKDGv3 starting conformer (random seed 61453), optimised in the gas phase with the GFN2-xTB semi-empirical method (tblite 0.4, ASE BFGS to 0.01 eV/A). A computed conformer, not a measured structure; small molecules come out within about 0.02 A of experiment (CO2 C=O 1.14 A against 1.16 A measured).
sources.ION-CLUSTER: Representative ion cluster, not a crystal structure: ions on a simple cubic grid, cations and anions alternating, spacing from the CRC density (the cube root of the volume per ion). Polyatomic ions are RDKit conformers (see RDKIT).
sources.ATOM: A single atom standing for one formula unit of a metal, covalent network solid or elemental lattice; spacing from the CRC density.
sources.COLOUR-GE: Greenwood and Earnshaw, 'Chemistry of the Elements', 2nd ed. (1997), the description of each substance; cross-checked against the Wikipedia article for that substance (appearance in its infobox).
sources.COLOUR-FLAME: Flame colours: Wikipedia, 'Flame test' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flame_test): lithium crimson, sodium yellow-orange, potassium lilac, calcium orange-red, strontium red, barium pale green, copper blue-green; magnesium burns with a brilliant white light (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnesium). Emission lines: NIST Atomic Spectra Database (Na 589.0 and 589.6 nm; Li 670.8 nm; K 766.5 and 769.9 nm, with 404.4 nm violet).
sources.COLOUR-HC: Hydrocarbon flames: Gaydon, 'The Spectroscopy of Flames', 2nd ed. (1974): the blue of a premixed flame is CH* (431 nm) and C2* Swan band (516 nm) emission; the yellow of a diffusion (candle) flame is glowing soot, close to a blackbody. Hydrogen and methanol burn with an almost invisible pale flame (OH* emits at 306 nm, in the ultraviolet).

s.how: Hf(g) -560.7 (API-TDB) minus Hvap(298 K) 128.2 (GHAZ) and Hfus 56.9 at the melting point (CRC-PC); the fusion term is not at 298 K and solid-solid transitions are left out, so this is an estimate.
Pure copper(II) carbonate is rarely made; the 'copper carbonate' sold is basic copper carbonate. Estimated: a value given for CuCO3 in older compilations, not in the CRC or NBS tables used here.

No standard value: pure NI3 is too unstable to measure (the real solid is the ammonia adduct NI3.NH3). Estimated from the decomposition enthalpy 2NI3 -> N2 + 3I2, about -290 kJ/mol, quoted by Wikipedia 'Nitrogen triiodide'.

g.described: colourless at bench strength (pale blue when concentrated)
